The Integrated Project Delivery Report details a recurring pattern of coordinated meetings across seven key project areas: site preparation, material procurement, health and safety, quality inspection, schedule coordination, stakeholder communication, and testing & commissioning. Each meeting follows the same structure: comparison with an approved plan, recording of field inspection evidence, assignment of follow-up actions to designated owners, and a discussion encompassing operational impact, cost, schedule, safety, communication, and user needs. Decisions are consistently based on verified observations rather than assumptions.

Dependencies involving procurement, testing, documentation, and handover are systematically identified. Responsible owners will update status registers with supporting photographic evidence, measurements, or correspondence. Risks requiring escalation are documented with a recommended action and deadline. The team actively evaluates the practicality of controls for each activity area, noting that a technically sound plan can fail due to unclear instructions, overlapping responsibilities, or delayed information. To mitigate this risk, reporting has been simplified, a single source of truth established, and changes verified before implementation. Future progress will be assessed via measurements of completion time, error frequency, user feedback, and unresolved issues.

The team implemented strategies to mitigate potential failures of technically correct plans, such as simplifying reporting, defining a single source of truth, and verifying critical changes before implementation. A recurring measure was the next cycle's assessment of completion time, error frequency, user feedback, and unresolved issues for consistent progress evaluation. Dependencies were identified involving procurement, testing, documentation, and handover.
